newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ AGAINST COUNTRY SPECIFIC WOOL QUOTA - SMITH.
newsitem.headline: NZ AGAINST COUNTRY SPECIFIC WOOL QUOTA - SMITH.

text.p: International Trade Minister Lockwood Smith said on Wednesday New Zealand had worked hard in its negotiations with China to ensure there was no country specific quota imposed on wool imports.

"We will not be guaranteed any part of the quota, and New Zealand worked hard to ensure there was not a country-specific tariff quota. That would not have been in New Zealand's interests," Smith said in parliament.
He said China had proposed New Zealand should be allocated seven percent of the tariff quota in wool tops, but had been persuaded to delete that from the agreement.
"So New Zealand has possible access to the full tariff quota and it depends on our competitiveness and our efficiency how much quota we achieve," Smith said.

China last week agreed to an import quota of 220,000 tonnes of wool fibre a year at a tariff of one percent, down from 10 percent, and will allow the amount to increase to 287,000 tonnes a year over seven years, a spokesman for Smith said.
He said the new quotas were well above current levels of imports to China. The tariff reductions would apply immediately and the quota come into force on January 1, 1998.
China is the largest market for New Zealand's wool trade.
